exposure: CRP levels (categorized as CRP-positive and CRP-negative)
outcome: neonatal morbidity (lower APGAR scores, perinatal depression)
cohort: 78 cases of Preterm Premature Rupture of Membranes (PPROM).
finding: Elevated C-reactive protein (CRP) levels correlated with higher maternal complications, increased neonatal morbidity, and longer NICU stays.
mod_finding: The CRP-positive group had more C-sections and labor inductions.
